name: Thames crossing, Plumstead - North Woolwich (Crossrail Thames Tunnel), London
description: Ground along the 2.3 km bored Thames Tunnel of the Elizabeth line from 15 open BGS/Crossrail boreholes, four of them over the river.
datum: m OD (ground levels of the logs; river-bed level for the over-water holes)
licence: Borehole data: Open Government Licence v3.0. Contains British Geological Survey materials (c) UKRI 2026. Contains public sector information licensed under the Open Government Licence v3.0. Line (c) OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL.

MG.name: Made Ground
MG.source: Chandegra & Kokkinou (2016), Crossrail Learning Legacy, Design of the deep cut-and-cover Crossrail Paddington Station, Table 1, https://learninglegacy.crossrail.co.uk/documents/design-deep-cut-cover-crossrail-paddington-station-using-finite-element-method/

AL.name: Alluvium
AL.source: Lawrence et al. (2015), Crossrail Learning Legacy, Variation in permeability and dewatering performance for part of the Crossrail route in east London, https://learninglegacy.crossrail.co.uk/documents/variation-permeability-dewatering-performance-part-crossrail-route-east-london-2/
AL.notes: Clay, silt and peat; k 1e-9 to 1e-8 m/s (Lawrence 4.3). No open strength or grading; assumed.

RTD.name: River Terrace Deposits (gravel)
RTD.source: Chandegra & Kokkinou (2016), Crossrail Learning Legacy, Design of the deep cut-and-cover Crossrail Paddington Station, Table 1, https://learninglegacy.crossrail.co.uk/documents/design-deep-cut-cover-crossrail-paddington-station-using-finite-element-method/; permeability Lawrence et al. (2015), Crossrail Learning Legacy, Variation in permeability and dewatering performance for part of the Crossrail route in east London, https://learninglegacy.crossrail.co.uk/documents/variation-permeability-dewatering-performance-part-crossrail-route-east-london-2/
RTD.notes: Sandy gravel up to about 5 m thick, k about 1e-3 m/s (Lawrence 2.3, 4.3). d10 assumed for a sandy gravel; no grading in the open logs.

LG.name: Lambeth Group (Upnor Formation)
LG.source: Entwisle et al. (2013), BGS OR/13/006, Engineering Geology of British Rocks and Soils: Lambeth Group, Table 6.7, https://nora.nerc.ac.uk/id/eprint/503110/
LG.notes: Upnor sand, shear box c' 8 kPa, phi' 33 deg (Table 6.7).

TS.name: Thanet Sand Formation
TS.source: Menkiti et al. (2015), Crossrail Learning Legacy, Geology and geotechnical properties of the Thanet Sand Formation, https://learninglegacy.crossrail.co.uk/documents/geology-geotechnical-properties-thanet-sand-formation-update-crossrail-project-2/
TS.notes: Bulk density 1.88-1.9 Mg/m3, peak phi' 37-39 deg at 400-700 kPa, c' 0 (4.1-4.2); fines 0-70 % (3), d10 assumed for a silty fine sand.

CK.name: Chalk (Seaford Chalk Formation)
CK.source: Lawrence et al. (2015), Crossrail Learning Legacy, Variation in permeability and dewatering performance for part of the Crossrail route in east London, https://learninglegacy.crossrail.co.uk/documents/variation-permeability-dewatering-performance-part-crossrail-route-east-london-2/ (formation, grades, permeability); Vinck et al. (2023), OSIG, Monotonic characterisation of low- to medium-density chalk, https://discovery.ucl.ac.uk/id/eprint/10200111/ (Seaford/Margate Chalk in Kent, analogue) (phi', K0)
CK.notes: Weak to moderately weak fractured chalk with flint bands (Seaford, CIRIA grades A to Dc/Dm). Critical-state phi' about 31 deg and K0 0.6 in the analogue tests. Excavated chalk is mostly finer than 40 um (T&T 2014); d10 2 um assumed. The fractured mass, not the grains, governs slurry loss at the face.

alignment.source: Assumed. Cover under the river 10-12 m and support above 3 bar under the river (Tunnels & Tunnelling (2014), Crossrail C310, https://tunnelsandtunnelling.com/?p=7323); the drive starts in gravel and Thanet Sand and meets Chalk about 100 m from launch, about 80 % in Chalk (Tunnels & Tunnelling (2014), Crossrail C310, https://tunnelsandtunnelling.com/?p=7323).

groundwater.source: Lawrence et al. (2015), Crossrail Learning Legacy, Variation in permeability and dewatering performance for part of the Crossrail route in east London, https://learninglegacy.crossrail.co.uk/documents/variation-permeability-dewatering-performance-part-crossrail-route-east-london-2/; Tunnels & Tunnelling (2014), Crossrail C310, https://tunnelsandtunnelling.com/?p=7323
groundwater.notes: Design groundwater 96.5-104.5 mATD, average 100.5 mATD (+0.5 m OD) (T&T). All units follow one water system. Tidal swing in the ground 0.4-0.7 m at North Woolwich, under 0.1 m at Plumstead (Lawrence 3.1, 3.4).

river.notes: Mean high water about +3.2 m OD and mean low water about -2.0 m OD at the Environment Agency Charlton gauge 0003 (about 3 km upstream; OGL), from one month of 15-minute readings, Oct-Nov 2026: estimates, not official MHWS/MLWS. The tide changed the face pressure by about 0.8 bar on the drive (Tunnels & Tunnelling (2014), Crossrail C310, https://tunnelsandtunnelling.com/?p=7323).
